subject: Clarify billing quantum and overspill behavior for mixed long-context calls
messages:
From: Anna Keller <anna.keller@clearhealth.io>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearhealth.io
Date: 2028-07-29T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Billing question: partial tokens + long-context overspill

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the ClearHealth team is excited about using Redwood for our patient summarization pipeline. Our procurement lead asked a follow-up on metering details that I couldn't answer off the top of my head. Two related questions: 

1) If a request contains a 22k-context prompt and the response writes back another 6k tokens (so total > model context), how are billing units counted across the overspill? In particular: do you charge the full context length for the request and then separately for the response? If the system auto-chunks the prompt, is each chunk rounded up to the billing quantum?

2) For streaming responses where the model emits tokens gradually and the client disconnects after the first 800 tokens — are partial streams billed pro-rata or rounded up to the minimum per-call quantum?

I've attached a spreadsheet with a few example call shapes from our end (ClearHealth_context_examples.xlsx). Can you provide an invoice-style sample showing how these would be billed? Also curious whether any negotiated seat/commit packaging would change rounding behavior (i.e., do committed tiers get finer granularity?).

Appreciate a clear worked example we can share with procurement.

Best,
Anna
Anna Keller
Director, ML Product
ClearHealth

[Attachment: ClearHealth_context_examples.xlsx (spreadsheet, ~48KB)]

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Billing question: partial tokens + long-context overspill

Hi Anna — thanks for the concrete examples, that helps. Quick summary up front, then I attached a sample invoice and a short worked example.

Short answers:
- We bill request and response tokens separately. If the request is internally split into chunks, each chunk is metered, but we only bill the actual tokens sent (we do not double-charge for overlap except where the customer explicitly pins multiple calls).
- Rounding/quantum: there is a minimum billing quantum of 64 token-units for hosted, applied per billed call unit. For committed enterprise tiers that buy Dedicated capacity, we can reduce the quantum to 8 tokens for high-volume streams as part of packaging.
- Streaming early disconnect: for hosted API calls, partial streams are rounded up to the quantum per-call (so 800 tokens would be rounded to the next 64-unit boundary). For Dedicated/commit customers we can apply per-call pro-rata billing or a smaller quantum — this is configurable in the contract.

I've attached a short invoice sample (redwood_pricing_summary_v2.pdf) and filled in three rows from your spreadsheet — see the worksheet named "Metering worked examples". A couple of notes on the examples: we treat KV cache reuse as a separate crediting mechanism (if your repeated requests hit cache, those tokens appear with a credit line).

I'll also loop Laura (pricing) and Sergio (solutions) on packaging options so we can show how a committed discount + reduced quantum affects your per-call bill.

Next steps: Laura can follow up with a packaging sketch and a committed quantum proposal. If helpful, we can produce a sample invoice using your actual call counts over a 30-day window.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Head of Sales — Platform
Redwood Inference

Anna — looping in a pragmatic packaging proposal. Short version: we can make two contract-level changes that materially reduce rounding friction for you:

1) Commit tier option: a monthly committed token pool with a 10% discount and reduced per-call quantum of 8 tokens for any endpoint designated as "high-throughput". That means each billed call will round to 8 tokens instead of 64. This is subject to a 3-month minimum.

2) Context overspill handling: for very long prompts where we perform internal chunking, we will report and bill per-byte/token actually executed; however, to avoid per-call churn on invoices we will auto-aggregate small remainder chunks under a single daily consolidation line with no additional rounding beyond the chosen quantum. Practically this removes tiny rounding noise for high volume batched requests.

Example (from your spreadsheet):
- Case A: single API call with 22k prompt + 6k response (model max 32k) => request split into 2 chunks for execution. Billed tokens: Sum(actual_request_tokens) rounded per chunk quantum + response tokens rounded per quantum. With committed quantum 8, rounding loss is negligible.

I'll prepare a two-month pro-forma invoice showing (a) hosted on-demand with 64-quantum and (b) committed pool with 8-quantum and the 10% discount so you can compare net spend. Sergio, can your team mock a 30-day sample trace using the examples Anna attached?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Principal, Commercial Pricing
Redwood Inference
